digitization: Converting an analog signal to digital data. (05a slide 6). See [Digitization and the PCM encoder](#/comp3721-w5/digitization-pcm).
PCM|pulse code modulation: The most commonly used technique for digitization. A PCM encoder has three processes: sampling, quantizing, encoding. See [Digitization and the PCM encoder](#/comp3721-w5/digitization-pcm).
A2D|ADC|analog-to-digital conversion: Converting an analog signal to digital data, as the microphone in a recorder does before storing PCM-encoded data. See [Digitization and the PCM encoder](#/comp3721-w5/digitization-pcm).
D2A|DAC|digital-to-analog conversion: Converting digital data to a bandpass analog signal by modifying the amplitude, frequency or phase of a carrier (modulation or shift keying). See [The carrier, ASK, FSK and PSK](#/comp3721-w5/ask-fsk-psk).
A2A|analog-to-analog conversion: Modulating an analog carrier with an analog modulating signal: AM, FM, PM. See [AM, FM and PM, and the radio bands](#/comp3721-w5/am-fm-pm).
sampling: The first step in PCM; the analog signal is sampled every T_s seconds. See [Sampling: T_s, f_s and the three methods](#/comp3721-w5/sampling-methods).
PAM|pulse amplitude modulation: Another name for the sampling process. See [Sampling: T_s, f_s and the three methods](#/comp3721-w5/sampling-methods).
Ts|sample interval|sample period: The analog signal is sampled every T_s seconds. See [Sampling: T_s, f_s and the three methods](#/comp3721-w5/sampling-methods).
fs|sampling rate|sampling frequency: f_s = 1/T_s, in samples per second. See [Sampling: T_s, f_s and the three methods](#/comp3721-w5/sampling-methods).
bandlimited: A signal with an infinite bandwidth cannot be sampled; the signal must be bandlimited. See [Sampling: T_s, f_s and the three methods](#/comp3721-w5/sampling-methods).
ideal sampling|impulse sampling: Instantaneous samples (stems); cannot be easily implemented. See [Sampling: T_s, f_s and the three methods](#/comp3721-w5/sampling-methods).
natural sampling: Uses a high-speed switch that rapidly connects and disconnects the signal path; the pulse top follows the signal. See [Sampling: T_s, f_s and the three methods](#/comp3721-w5/sampling-methods).
flat-top sampling|sample-and-hold: Uses a circuit that holds the sampled value; the most commonly used method. See [Sampling: T_s, f_s and the three methods](#/comp3721-w5/sampling-methods).
Nyquist theorem: To reproduce the original analog signal, the sampling rate must be at least 2 times the highest frequency contained in the signal. See [The Nyquist theorem and the sampling rate](#/comp3721-w5/nyquist-sampling).
fN|Nyquist rate: f_N = 2 f_max (Hz). See [The Nyquist theorem and the sampling rate](#/comp3721-w5/nyquist-sampling).
Nyquist interval: 1/f_N = 1/(2 f_max) seconds. See [The Nyquist theorem and the sampling rate](#/comp3721-w5/nyquist-sampling).
fmax|highest frequency: For a low-pass analog signal, bandwidth = highest frequency; for a bandpass analog signal, bandwidth < highest frequency, so the minimum sampling rate cannot be found from the bandwidth alone. See [The Nyquist theorem and the sampling rate](#/comp3721-w5/nyquist-sampling).
oversampling: Sampling above the Nyquist rate (f_s = 4f in the figure): the same approximation but redundant and unnecessary. See [The Nyquist theorem and the sampling rate](#/comp3721-w5/nyquist-sampling).
undersampling: Sampling below the Nyquist rate (f_s = f in the figure): produces a signal that does not look like the original one. See [The Nyquist theorem and the sampling rate](#/comp3721-w5/nyquist-sampling).
quantization|quantizing: The set of amplitudes (can be infinite with nonintegral values) is mapped to a set of discrete values; an approximation process. See [Quantization: zones, midpoints, codes, error](#/comp3721-w5/quantization).
L|quantization levels|zones: The number of zones the range V_min to V_max is divided into; codes 0 to L − 1 are assigned to the midpoints. In audio digitizing, L = 256. See [Quantization: zones, midpoints, codes, error](#/comp3721-w5/quantization).
Δ|delta|zone height: Δ = (V_max − V_min)/L, the height of each zone. See [Quantization: zones, midpoints, codes, error](#/comp3721-w5/quantization).
normalized PAM value: Actual amplitude divided by Δ (e.g. −6.1/5 = −1.22). See [Quantization: zones, midpoints, codes, error](#/comp3721-w5/quantization).
normalized quantized value: The midpoint of the zone the normalized PAM value falls in (−1.22 is in zone 2, midpoint −1.50). See [Quantization: zones, midpoints, codes, error](#/comp3721-w5/quantization).
normalized error|quantization error|quan: The difference between the normalized quantized value and the normalized PAM value; −Δ/2 ≤ quantization error ≤ Δ/2. See [Quantization: zones, midpoints, codes, error](#/comp3721-w5/quantization).
quantization code: The zone number 0 to L − 1 of a sample. See [Quantization: zones, midpoints, codes, error](#/comp3721-w5/quantization).
encoding: The last step of PCM: each quantized sample is changed to an n_b-bit code word. See [Encoding, bits per sample and the bit rate](#/comp3721-w5/encoding-bit-rate).
nb|bits per sample: n_b = log₂ L. See [Encoding, bits per sample and the bit rate](#/comp3721-w5/encoding-bit-rate).
bit rate (PCM): Bit rate = sampling rate × number of bits per sample = f_s × n_b. See [Encoding, bits per sample and the bit rate](#/comp3721-w5/encoding-bit-rate).
SNRdB (quantization): SNR_dB = 6.02 n_b + 1.76 dB, the contribution of the quantization error; more levels, higher SNR, higher Shannon capacity. See [Quantization error, nonuniform quantization and PCM bandwidth](#/comp3721-w5/quantization-error-bandwidth).
uniform quantization: Fixed Δ; only optimal for a uniformly distributed signal. See [Quantization error, nonuniform quantization and PCM bandwidth](#/comp3721-w5/quantization-error-bandwidth).
nonuniform quantization: Δ is not fixed; the slide: greater near the lower amplitudes and less near the higher amplitudes. See [Quantization error, nonuniform quantization and PCM bandwidth](#/comp3721-w5/quantization-error-bandwidth).
Bmin|PCM bandwidth: B_min = c × n_b × 2 × B_analog × 1/r; with c = 1/2 and r = 1, B_min = n_b × B_analog: n_b times the analog bandwidth, the price we pay for digitization. See [Quantization error, nonuniform quantization and PCM bandwidth](#/comp3721-w5/quantization-error-bandwidth).
carrier signal|carrier frequency|fc: A high-frequency sine wave produced by the sending device that acts as a base for the information signal; the receiver is tuned to its frequency. See [The carrier, ASK, FSK and PSK](#/comp3721-w5/ask-fsk-psk).
modulation|shift keying: Modifying the amplitude, frequency or phase of the carrier based on the digital data. See [The carrier, ASK, FSK and PSK](#/comp3721-w5/ask-fsk-psk).
ASK|amplitude shift keying: The amplitude of the carrier is varied to create signal elements; frequency and phase remain constant. B = (1 + d)S. See [The carrier, ASK, FSK and PSK](#/comp3721-w5/ask-fsk-psk).
BASK|OOK|on-off keying: Binary ASK with two levels: peak amplitude 0 for one signal element and the carrier's peak amplitude for the other. See [The carrier, ASK, FSK and PSK](#/comp3721-w5/ask-fsk-psk).
d: The factor in B = (1 + d)S; not defined on the slides (the textbook: between 0 and 1, depending on modulation and filtering, unverified). See [The carrier, ASK, FSK and PSK](#/comp3721-w5/ask-fsk-psk).
FSK|frequency shift keying: The frequency of the carrier is changed to represent data; peak amplitude and phase constant. B = (1 + d)S + 2Δf. See [The carrier, ASK, FSK and PSK](#/comp3721-w5/ask-fsk-psk).
BFSK: Two carrier frequencies: f₁ for data element 0, f₂ for data element 1, each Δf from the midpoint between the two bands; implemented with a voltage-controlled oscillator. See [The carrier, ASK, FSK and PSK](#/comp3721-w5/ask-fsk-psk).
Δf: Half the difference between f₁ and f₂ in BFSK; the two frequencies differ by 2Δf. See [The carrier, ASK, FSK and PSK](#/comp3721-w5/ask-fsk-psk).
VCO|voltage-controlled oscillator: The block that implements BFSK. See [The carrier, ASK, FSK and PSK](#/comp3721-w5/ask-fsk-psk).
PSK|phase shift keying: The phase of the carrier is changed to represent signal elements; peak amplitude and frequency constant. More common than ASK or FSK; less susceptible to noise because noise can change the amplitude easier than it can change the phase; needs more sophisticated hardware. See [The carrier, ASK, FSK and PSK](#/comp3721-w5/ask-fsk-psk).
BPSK: Two signal elements, phases 0° and 180°; the same bandwidth as BASK but less than BFSK. See [The carrier, ASK, FSK and PSK](#/comp3721-w5/ask-fsk-psk).
QAM|quadrature amplitude modulation: Combines ASK and PSK; the dominant method of digital-to-analog modulation; two carriers, one in-phase and one quadrature (90° apart), with different peak amplitudes; the same minimum bandwidth as ASK and PSK; used in 802.11 Wi-Fi. See [QAM and constellation diagrams](#/comp3721-w5/constellation).
in-phase carrier|I: The X axis of a constellation diagram. See [QAM and constellation diagrams](#/comp3721-w5/constellation).
quadrature carrier|Q: The Y axis of a constellation diagram; 90° out of phase with the in-phase carrier. See [QAM and constellation diagrams](#/comp3721-w5/constellation).
constellation diagram: A representation of a signal modulated by a digital modulation scheme; each signal element type is a dot; the length from the origin is the amplitude and the angle is the phase. A modulation with n constellation points transmits log₂ n bits per signal element. See [QAM and constellation diagrams](#/comp3721-w5/constellation).
n-QAM|16-QAM: n constellation points carrying log₂ n bits per symbol: 16-QAM 4 bits, 64-QAM 6, 256-QAM 8, 1024-QAM 10, 4K-QAM 12. See [QAM and constellation diagrams](#/comp3721-w5/constellation).
AM|amplitude modulation: The carrier's amplitude varies with the modulating signal; frequency and phase remain the same. B_AM = 2B, centred on the carrier frequency; AM radio stations get 10 kHz (5 kHz audio). See [AM, FM and PM, and the radio bands](#/comp3721-w5/am-fm-pm).
FM|frequency modulation: The carrier's frequency follows the modulating signal's amplitude; peak amplitude and phase constant. B_FM = 2(1 + β)B; FM stations get 200 kHz (15 kHz stereo audio, β = 4, 50 kHz guard band). See [AM, FM and PM, and the radio bands](#/comp3721-w5/am-fm-pm).
β|beta: The FM factor in B_FM = 2(1 + β)B; β = 4 for FM radio. See [AM, FM and PM, and the radio bands](#/comp3721-w5/am-fm-pm).
PM|phase modulation: The carrier's phase follows the modulating signal's amplitude; peak amplitude and frequency fixed. See [AM, FM and PM, and the radio bands](#/comp3721-w5/am-fm-pm).
modulating signal: The information signal (e.g. audio) that modulates the carrier in AM, FM and PM. See [AM, FM and PM, and the radio bands](#/comp3721-w5/am-fm-pm).
guard band (FM): The extra 50 kHz in the 200 kHz FM allocation. See [AM, FM and PM, and the radio bands](#/comp3721-w5/am-fm-pm).
